# Repository Instructions

This file is the entry point for agent instructions in this repository.
Workflows and policies live in the documents under `docs/agents/`; the domain
vocabulary lives in `CONTEXT.md` at the root.

## Testing and Verification

Tests are part of the specification. Write the failing test first at the
spec's pre-agreed seams and make it green with the minimal change — red
before green, one seam, one test, one slice per cycle — per the build
discipline in [docs/agents/issue-tracker.md](docs/agents/issue-tracker.md).
Test-after is reserved for glue and wiring, UI verified by a manual test plan,
and throwaway prototypes. During implementation and review, run the focused
checks recorded under Agent skills for the changed areas and their immediate
contracts; the epic gate recorded there is reserved for the final integrated
epic commit before acceptance and closure.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Gitea issues, driven by the `gitea-issues` helpers.
See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Canonical role names mapped to this tracker's label strings.
See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

single layout: CONTEXT.md and ADRs live per `docs/agents/domain.md`.

### Work queue

Priority lives in the `type/roadmap` issue's ordered queue; see `docs/agents/queue.md`.

### Working standards

Docs and tests are first-class artifacts; the tracker is the queue, repository
documents the durable memory. Read the issue's epic and related issues
before planning; build test-first at the spec's pre-agreed seams; record each
change's documentation disposition and the evidence behind its merge; commands
presented as runnable must be ready to run as written. See
`docs/agents/standards.md`.

### Focused checks

`uv run --locked pytest tests/<area>`

Run on the exact current head during implementation and review follow-ups;
any later change makes this evidence stale.

### Epic gate

`make check`

The complete gate, reserved for final epic acceptance — run once on the exact
integrated commit. On an execution host, run it as
`scripts/execution_host.py gate`, which runs `make check` in a dedicated
checkout at the staged checkout's exact commit and keeps a receipt (see
`docs/runbooks/portable-execution-host.md`, "Run the gate").

## Install

Use Linux, Python 3.12+, Node 22.19+ and Docker/Compose. The repository pins
Inspect AI 0.3.261 and Inspect Evals 0.16.0. Its dependency commands require uv
0.12.9; if the host uv differs, use `uvx --from uv==0.12.9 uv` in place of `uv`.

```sh
uv sync --locked
npm ci --ignore-scripts
```

The independently pinned Codex/Muse runtime requires the existing
[build/install procedure](docs/runbooks/codex-muse-runtime.md).
Do not replace it with stock Codex. Dependencies must be available inside the
checkout mounted by Docker; symlinking `node_modules` outside it is insufficient.

## Provider-free checks

```sh
uv run --locked python -m pytest -q tests/test_shakedown_matrix.py tests/test_qualification_inputs.py -m 'not benchmark_docker'
uv run --locked python scripts/package_swe_bench_tasks.py --check
uv run --locked python scripts/run_shakedown_matrix.py --help
```

The qualification runbook lists native/Inspect/recovery checks and the explicit
Docker gold/unchanged controls. `make check` remains the full repository gate;
use focused checks while developing a bounded change. Neither mock credentials
nor provider-free tests authorize a live run.

## Native products and research

- [Native research clients and probes](docs/runbooks/native-research-clients.md)
- [OpenCode adapter](docs/runbooks/opencode-adapter.md)
- [Claude Code adapter](docs/runbooks/claude-code-adapter.md)

# Native research clients v2

Prospective allocations are governed by the owner-approved [shared research budget v2](../contracts/shared-research-budget-v2.md). Use the same doubled work limits across all shared arms; historical runs below retain their original budgets. New-policy claims require fresh admission and execution.

Documentation disposition: **updated** for #71 and the [v2 admission suite and probe](research-admission-v2.md) from #72. The seven standard native arms
consume `NativeResearch` from `agent_harness_evals/native_research.py`. RelayView
continues to use its owner wrapper (#64 / RelayView #330). Exact v2 assignments,
model routes and future admission gates are in the
[historical unified v2 contract](../contracts/unified-benchmark-v2.md). Prospective
admission consumes the exact arm set in the
[staged MultiLang v3 contract](../contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v3.md): six
standard clients for Stage A and the selected standard plus RelayView clients for
Stage B.

This delivery establishes deterministic native client integration, not actual
Brave/OpenAI search availability, paid provider compatibility or cohort admission.
No live model/research call or benchmark was run. #72 and #65 retain those gates.
The local Responses double substitutes transport and fixture authentication only;
it cannot attest the production credential, endpoint or provider model. Sol's
fixture uses a local catalog to avoid contacting the hosted catalog service.

## Versioned setup

Existing `experiment_arms/` manifests and the default adapter calls retain their
historical Stage 1 behavior. Opt in by supplying `research=` to `codex_config`,
`codex_cli_solver`, `opencode_config` or `opencode_cli_solver`. The binding must
match the manifest's exact arm ID. This creates `native-research-v4` evidence with
the configuration, route, model, reasoning, artifact and trusted service setup
digests. Retain this evidence beside the arm and whole-cohort manifests; any
different configuration/artifact/policy requires new admission and a new cohort.
Do not resume or pool a historical default-config, v2 or v3 run as v4. The existing unified
cohort admission validator still rejects production dispatch until its later
owners deliver admission; this integration adds no bypass.

For ordinary or historical Codex/Sol use `NativeResearch("codex-gpt-5.6-sol")`:
native `web_search="live"`, no shared service. For the Stage A profile, construct
the binding with `NativeResearch.from_service(service)` exactly like the other
five standard arms. That generated config sets `web_search="disabled"` and exposes
only the pinned `mcp__research` `web_search` and `web_fetch` tools. The two exact
inventories are frozen separately; selecting neither profile implicitly is not
allowed. Ranking, cache and physical work remain native-managed and unobserved
(`null`) only on the historical native path; no native/shared ranking parity is claimed. Settings are
checked against the pinned CLI, with the official
[Codex configuration reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)
as supporting documentation.

For Stage A Codex/Sol, Codex/GLM, Codex/Muse, all three OpenCode arms, and
Claude Code, keep a
`ResearchSidecar` context alive for the entire workflow and construct
`NativeResearch.from_service(service)` after readiness. The factory rejects a
stopped service, wrong arm, artifact or setup digest. Use the same binding for
configuration and result evidence. No client accepts provider keys, policy edits,
budgets, retry controls or role substitution through tool arguments.

The trusted runner's `_credentialed_sandbox(..., research_service=service)` merges
the package, Node binary, immutable Python launcher and **agent role socket directory** readonly into its
existing restricted model-provider Compose topology. It verifies trial identity,
exact provider endpoint, installed package hashes, Node 22.19.0, UID and modes.
It keeps the internal provider network and proxy and adds no public egress.
The container retains the runner's root user and existing capabilities so the
SWE-bench sanitizer can create its temporary repository beside `/testbed` and the
agent can read its leased credential and edit the checkout. Added `SETUID` and
`SETGID` capabilities let only the MCP launcher clear supplementary groups, assume
the socket owner's UID/GID, and exec the pinned bridge with an empty environment.
The Claude sandbox additionally retains only `CAP_KILL`, allowing its root
process-group supervisor to terminate and reap that intentionally cross-UID MCP
descendant; other arms do not receive it.
The released bridge still enforces socket ownership. No host home, database, research setup,
lock or Brave credential is mounted. Provision package/runtime before starting
the sandbox; do not install packages through an agent shell. Stop and prove the
native sandbox quiescent before leaving the sidecar context. Sidecar deadlines,
account/work ledgers and restart conservation remain owned by #70.

The shared bridge command inside the container is:

```zsh
python3 -I /opt/research-client.py
```

Codex's only declared MCP server is `research`, required at startup with exactly
`web_search` and `web_fetch`; native search is disabled for its GLM/Muse arms.
OpenCode uses its native local MCP configuration and denies built-in `webfetch`,
`websearch` and `codesearch` both globally and in every built-in agent. The build-agent
override is necessary in pinned OpenCode; a global denial alone leaves webfetch
in the model inventory. Existing isolated homes, strict Codex configuration,
OpenCode project-config/external-skill/default-plugin disablement and approved
pair transport observers continue to apply. Tool restrictions are not a network
sandbox: the Compose provider allowlist and readonly mounts enforce that boundary.
The [issue #101 runbook](opencode-glm-research-shakedown.md) binds these controls,
the common budget, and the live sidecar lifecycle into the five-project
OpenCode/GLM qualification path.

The OpenCode solver installs a required discovery gate alongside its pair observer.
Before the first task model request is sent, the gate requires the complete frozen
parent inventory. Later requests must match that inventory or one of two pinned
native Task inventories: `general` omits `task`, and `explore` omits both `task` and
`todowrite`. Every other tool, schema and description must still match exactly,
including both research tools. These are permitted inventory shapes; the gate
does not infer or claim the request's agent identity from its tool list. Missing, extra,
duplicate or changed tools latch a failure and block native retries. Auxiliary
requests without tools are blocked until discovery succeeds. After execution, the
solver independently checks identity-bound digest receipts; absent or failed
receipts reject admission with `research_discovery_failed`. Valid discovery still
does not establish live admission. Version 4 evidence binds launcher, gate and
all allowed inventory digests as well as configuration. Receipts retain the
observed digests, require parent discovery first, and never discard a failed
child request when the parent resumes.

## Output, discovery and evidence

The service retains at most four initial structural chunks, three explicitly
requested continuation chunks, eight continuations, 120 KiB cumulative document
bytes, 128 KiB canonical model-visible results and a 1 MiB MCP envelope. Native
clients never re-rank, clip service successes, retry or reset these counters.
An oversized service serialization is a typed `oversized_response` failure.

Codex's history output limit is explicitly 131072 tokens, allowing room for the
native envelope around the canonical byte ceiling. OpenCode's explicit
`tool_output.max_bytes=1048576` and `max_lines=2000` avoid its default 51200-byte
clipping of MCP text. Canonical JSON has escaped embedded newlines. These are
native wrapper settings, separate from document bytes and the core's initial vs
continuation selection. They also affect other native tool output and must be
included in the frozen config digest. These implementation ceilings do not approve
the benchmark's later resource allocation.

`fixtures/research-native/` freezes complete **fixture** model-visible tool
inventories, including native descriptions, schemas and namespace structure, for
each standard arm. Codex 0.144.0 presents research under the `mcp__research`
namespace; OpenCode 1.18.28 exposes `research_web_search` and `research_web_fetch`.
`verify_inventory` requires an independently frozen expected inventory and rejects
missing/extra/changed tools and disabled Sol live search. Never feed the current
inventory as its own expected value in admission. Production #72 must freeze its
actual exact-route inventory separately, including the declared transport observers.

Solver diagnostics deliberately say `discovery=not_observed`,
`researchCapable=false`, `liveAdmission=false` until independent native observations
are available. Task/pair success, a model's claim, an MCP config entry or service
readiness is not research admission. Fixtures observe the actual model request
and round-trip results. Later admission must additionally record actual search,

## Declared runtime requirements

| Repository | Node engine | Python / uv |
|---|---|---|
| **RelayView** | `>=22.19 <23 || >=24.11 <25` in `package.json` and the root entry of `package-lock.json`. Its README repeats these ranges. | No Python or uv requirement is declared for the root npm package. Some scripts and optional components invoke Python; their requirements are specific to those tasks, not a single root-level runtime declaration. |
| **agent-harness-evals** | `>=22.19.0` in `package.json` and its lockfile root entry. | `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` require Python `>=3.12`; `.python-version` selects `3.12`. The project requires **uv `==0.12.9`** (`tool.uv.required-version`); the README gives `uvx --from uv==0.12.9 uv` as an alternative when host uv differs. |

**The declared Node overlap is Node 22 from 22.19.0 onward, and Node 24 from 24.11.0 onward.** RelayView excludes Node 23 and Node 25; agent-harness-evals’ broader Node lower bound does not change that intersection.

## Relevant locked dependencies

- **RelayView browser tests:** `@playwright/test`, `playwright`, and `playwright-core` are all locked at **1.62.1**. Its native SQLite dependency, `better-sqlite3`, is locked at **13.0.3** and has an install script. These are npm lockfile resolutions; the Playwright browser binaries are a separate installation concern.
- **agent-harness-evals native CLI/runtime packages:** the npm manifest pins Claude Code **2.1.270**, Pi **0.85.0**, Codex **0.144.0**, and OpenCode **1.18.28** (`opencode-ai` and `@opencode-ai/plugin`). The lockfile resolves these versions and records platform-specific optional packages where applicable.
- **agent-harness-evals Python environment:** `pyproject.toml` pins Inspect AI **0.3.261**, Inspect Evals **0.16.0**, `jsonschema` **4.26.0**, and SWE-bench **3.0.15**; dev dependency pytest is **9.1.1**. `uv.lock` records the resolved packages and artifacts for the locked environment.

## What this establishes—and what it doesn’t

The manifests establish the projects’ declared engine and interpreter constraints, direct dependency specifications, and—alongside their lockfiles—the chosen npm/Python dependency resolutions. Lock entries also record details such as package integrity and, for some packages, engine or platform metadata.

They do **not** prove that installation or execution succeeds on a particular host. In particular, a real install/test is needed to check native-module installation, platform-specific CLI binaries, Playwright browser availability and system libraries, and the Python environment on the target platform. The evals README additionally calls for Linux and Docker/Compose; those are operational requirements beyond the Node engine declaration. No install or test was run for this comparison.

The supplied workspace trees do not include `.git` metadata, so I can compare their checked-in metadata and lockfiles but cannot independently verify the pinned commit hashes.
